page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance runs on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon processor operating at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. This hardware setup consists of 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 threads. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 55 MB of L3 cache. It features dedicated CPU allocation but does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-standard-2 in the lower tiers of performance. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as weak, falling in the bottom 25% with a score of 1103.39, while multi-core performance falls into the bottom 10% with a score of 1451.58. Memory bandwidth tests show poor throughput, measuring 11.77 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 10.27 GB/sec for large block write operations. Similarly, database operations and web serving throughput are limited, with static web serving reaching 1.45 GB/sec and Redis SET operations executing at 1.35 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the e2-standard-2 is its low computational and memory throughput in exchange for resource-density cost efficiency. It is designed as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require high-performance computing or high-speed memory access. Given its performance profile, the instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, such as basic web serving, small-scale development or testing environments, and low-traffic application hosting.

Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with dedicated CPU allocation, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance operates in the lower tiers, with stress-ng single-core performance in the bottom 25% and multi-core performance in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large block reads and writes averaging around 11 GB/sec. Consequently, the e2-standard-2 is positioned as a cost-efficient option for low-intensity workloads. It is best suited for basic web serving, small development environments, and lightweight background tasks that do not demand high-performance computing.
